figure_options._doc: Questions whose OPTIONS are diagrams rather than text. The red mark still identifies the answer; the option bodies are supplied as cropped images. The four labels MUST be listed explicitly: text extraction only finds whichever labels happen to sit on a text baseline, which left teh-074 offering a) and c) alone while its correct answer was b) — unanswerable. WARNING: the answers here are typed in by hand, and three of the original four were typed WRONG (see the per-question reasons). Never take one on trust; read the red label off the rendered page. To re-check all four at once, list the coloured spans that fall between a question's stem and the next question's stem.

teh-075.reason: Was 'c'. The red label on str. 12 is (d) — the response flat to 3 kHz then rolling off, i.e. the low-pass a microphone stage wants. Option (c) is a U-shaped curve. Physics and the red mark agree; the 'c' was a transcription slip when these four were hand-entered.

teh-095.reason: Was 'a'. The red label on str. 14 is b) — separated positive humps with gaps, which is what a half-wave rectifier actually produces. Option (a) is an un-rectified full sine.

teh-114.reason: Was 'a'. The red label on str. 16 is (c) — the modulation trapezoid whose edge runs past the apex, the signature of over 100 % modulation. Option (a) is a clean trapezoid, i.e. correct modulation.
